doc: The single source of truth for this domain's operator credentials.

`engine env doctor|setup|env-example --domain <domain>` all DERIVE from this file, so the thing built to fight onboarding drift does not itself drift. Edit here; never hand-edit .env.example (regenerate it).
key       env var name (or a synthetic BIN_*/mcp-server name for non-env rows)

required  req | triage | boards | optional. req -> a missing one FAILS the doctor (non-zero exit; gates callers). triage -> needed only when a wave hits the read-only DB (WARN). boards -> needed only to publish Decision/Outcomes boards (WARN). optional -> nice-to-have (WARN).
secret    true -> never seeded, never written to a committed file
default   non-secret default value (seeded into `dotfile` if absent), or null

dotfile   PREFERRED gitignored home — where a FRESH value is written (doctor seed / setup wizard); secrets are only ever written to .env.local. NOT the only place it is read: every file-key row resolves .env.local -> .env (project dotfiles only). A row stays on .env only when an out-of-band reader is pinned to it.
how       one-line how-to-get / fix hint (printed on a miss)

check     {type: file-key | env-present | binary(+name) | mcp(+server) | note}. file-key: env var set OR a searched dotfile contains KEY= (seedable if non-secret + default). env-present: env var set only. binary: `command -v <name>` succeeds. mcp: `claude mcp list` shows <server> Connected. note: informational only — never pass/fail, never affects exit code.
source    {type: prompt | oauth | aws-secret(+name[,field,region,profile])} — where a value COMES FROM when it is missing.

`<person>` in a source.name is substituted at fetch time with the operator's own agent name (from FINCH_AGENT_AWS_PROFILE, else inferred). It is what makes the login secret PER-PERSON, so an agent policy can grant GetSecretValue on its own login and nobody else's.

credentials.how: Create a Slack app + bot token with scopes chat:write, channels:read, groups:read; paste the xoxb- token into .env.local (fallback env: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN)
Fallback announce channel NAME (e.g. #intake). Per-project channels come from INBOX_REGISTRY; this is only a default
Lookback window (days) for the Phase-1 channel-context read (engine slack-read --history). Per-project override; the channel LIST lives in the project Inbox Handbook
Interactive OAuth in Claude Code: add the Linear HTTP MCP (mcp.linear.app/mcp) and complete browser consent. All /intake WRITES (save_comment, save_status_update, documents) are MCP-only

The NAME of the AWS profile holding your agent key, e.g. yarik-agent. A name only — no credential material ever enters the engine's storage; the key itself lives in ~/.aws/credentials, AWS's own store. Written for you by `engine env setup --aws-key <path>` (delivered key) or by `engine env provision --apply` (self-service). The agent profile deliberately has NO ~/.aws/config entry: the ABSENCE of login_session is what makes it never expire and never prompt for MFA
Run `aws sso login --profile <name>` for the staging profile, then export AWS_PROFILE. Gates the read-only DB tunnel (scripts/staging-db-tunnel.sh) used by triage
AWS region for the staging profile (default us-east-2)
Install AWS CLI v2 — the `aws` binary is required by scripts/staging-db-tunnel.sh
Install session-manager-plugin (Session Manager plugin) — required alongside aws for the SSM port-forward tunnel

EC2 Name tag of the bastion the read-only DB tunnel port-forwards through (scripts/staging-db-tunnel.sh discovers it by this tag; BASTION_INSTANCE_ID overrides). Declared as a TAG, not an instance id, because the id changes whenever the bastion is replaced — and because `engine env provision` derives the ssm:StartSession grant from it, conditioning on the tag rather than pinning a resource that will rot

Secrets Manager secret NAME holding the read-only data_ro postgres URL. Fetched at runtime (aws secretsmanager get-secret-value), host re-pointed to 127.0.0.1:15432. NEVER stored in a dotfile. Runbook: docs/runbooks/staging-db-ro-analyst.md
S3 bucket for published Decision/Outcomes boards
S3 region for board publish
S3 key prefix for board publish

OVERRIDE ONLY — leave it unset. The profile now comes from the one the doctor provisions (FINCH_AGENT_AWS_PROFILE), so publishing uses the same per-person agent credential as everything else: attributable to a person, revocable per person, and never expiring. Two ways to name an AWS identity was the duplication — one provisioned, one hand-set — and the hand-set one pointed at an SSO profile that expired daily. Set this only to override deliberately, and CLEAR it on instance credentials, where naming a profile shadows the credentials that should be used.
Key prefix under the proofs bucket for board STATE objects (skills/prove/assets/state-append.sh writes <prefix>/<doc>.json; prove-sync folds events into it). Default state
Key prefix for the append-only board EVENT objects that skills/prove/assets/prove-sync.sh folds into state. Default events
OPTIONAL per-user key segment for published boards (skills/prove/assets/publish-s3.sh). Leave unset to derive it from the AWS caller identity — there is deliberately no default
Temporal host (temporal.<env>.finch.local) for the optional visibility tunnel; not on the core intake path
Temporal port (default 7233) for the optional visibility tunnel
Interactive OAuth for the Notion HTTP MCP (mcp.notion.com/mcp). Only needed at project creation / KB maintenance. No CLI fallback

Interactive OAuth for the PostHog MCP in Claude Code (user-scoped, so it is visible from every project). Sources product-analytics signals during triage. Supersedes the old 'UNWIRED / handled manually via the PostHog UI' note — there IS an automated path now, and no CLI fallback
Interactive OAuth for the GitHub MCP in Claude Code (project-scoped). Lets a wave read the PRs/issues an inbox signal cites. Not on the core intake path — /intake never writes to GitHub

⚠️ THE LOGIN IS PLUS-ADDRESSED — <name>+agent@finchclaims.com, never <name>-agent@. Sub-addressing delivers to the person's existing inbox, so no new mailbox is needed; a dash address would require one, and the identity provider sends verification and reset mail there, making the account unrecoverable the first time that matters. The DASH form stays correct for the IAM user, the AWS profile and the secret path — none of those deliver mail. Created by `engine env provision` directly at the restricted `agent` role, NEVER super_admin: no account was ever made at super_admin, so that bridge is SKIPPED rather than dismantled. WHAT `agent` MEANS: it reads across organisations (target org supplied per request, no allowlist — any org, including the largest customer books) and is refused on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. ⚠️ That is NOT the same as 'it cannot write' — a few GET endpoints write as a side effect, so do not describe this account as unable to write. A write-capable `super_agent` role is deferred; the lane ships read-only. ⚠️ THESE CREDENTIALS ARE SHAPED FOR A HUMAN HOLDER — an accountable person, on their own machine, revoked by one call. The AWS key deliberately never expires and this password lands in .env.local in plaintext: right for that case, wrong for an unattended one. BEFORE HANDING THIS TO A NON-HUMAN the deferred controls become required — short-lived grants instead of a standing key, workload OIDC so no secret is stored, a broker holding the real credential, approval per claim. Note 'staging' in the path is not a lower environment: staging IS production. Per-person, never shared — that is what buys attribution, revocation and per-person secret scoping. This row is the login EMAIL of your own <name>+agent account. Fetched from Secrets Manager, never typed.

This row is the PASSWORD for your own <name>+agent account. Fetched from Secrets Manager, never typed, and only your own agent policy can read it.

⚠️ PROVISIONER ONLY — an agent must NEVER hold this. Secrets Manager secret NAME holding the READ-WRITE app database URL. Needed once per person, to insert the app `user` row that gives a provisioned agent its role; without that row the account authenticates and the application still does not know it. Reached through the SSM tunnel like the read-only one, and NEVER written to a dotfile. The `provisioner` tier exists precisely so this row can be declared here without the policy derivation ever being able to grant it.

organization_id for a provisioned agent's app `user` row. The column is NOT NULL with a foreign key, while an agent redirects its organisation per request — so its home org is arbitrary in meaning but must still be a real row. This is Summit Ridge, the temporary internal org. It lives here rather than in code so it can be changed without a release, and so the value is discoverable next to the thing that consumes it.

The setup guide a newly provisioned person is pointed at when their key is delivered. Declared here rather than written into the delivery code so the link can be corrected without a release — a dead onboarding link is discovered by the one person least able to work around it.

Local port the SSM tunnel to the app database listens on (scripts/staging-db-tunnel.sh, LOCAL_PORT). The database is not reachable directly, so provisioning an app row goes through it. 15432 rather than 5432 so a local Postgres is never shadowed.
